files.refuter_finding:
The TAKE-MINE verdict is wrong on two checkable points; broken_on_head is correctly true but under-stated.

1) THEIRS carries signing-layer behavior HEAD does NOT subsume, and it is not a "follow-up ticket". HEAD's own docstring says the canonicalizer RAISES: /srv/ws/salesagent/a3-9421-on-1721/src/core/schemas/_base.py, "Raises: TargetUriMalformedError: For an authority the profile requires be rejected rather than canonicalized (no host, bare IPv6, unclosed bracket, IPv6 zone id)." (confirmed in src/core/signing/canonical.py: reject_malformed_target + _delegated re-raise). HEAD then calls it UNGUARDED in two places inside _validate_and_convert_format_ids:
   - `registered_agent_urls = {canonical_agent_url(agent.agent_url) for agent in registered_agents}` (HEAD side of the conflict at ~line 1793-1802)
   - `agent_url = canonical_agent_url(validated_fmt.agent_url)` (~line 1829, outside any try)
TargetUriMalformedError is a SignatureVerificationError/ValueError, NOT an AdCPError, so on HEAD a single malformed registered agent_url, or a buyer-supplied agent_url whose authority the comparer profile rejects (IPv6 zone id, unclosed bracket — shapes pydantic AnyUrl admits), escapes uncaught: an ungraded 500 instead of a graded AdCP error, and for the registered-set case ONE bad admin-ingested row breaks EVERY format_id validation for that tenant. THEIRS added exactly these two guards with that reasoning: `_build_registered_agent_urls` (skip + warn the malformed registration, "#1291") and `_normalize_incoming_agent_url` (translate to AdCPValidationError with the "Package N, format_ids[idx]" context). That is a signing-induced new failure mode created by routing identity comparison through the 9421 canonicalizer — it must survive, re-expressed on #1721's shape: keep HEAD's canonical_agent_url and HEAD's typed errors, but wrap the set comprehension in try/except TargetUriMalformedError (skip + log) and wrap the incoming call so it raises AdCPValidationError(field=field, details=ValidationDetails(**where, agent_url=...), internal_detail=e) — no `message=`, no dict details.

2) Resolving the conflict hunks to OURS is NOT sufficient, because THEIRS' two helpers landed OUTSIDE the conflict markers and are sitting in the working tree right now at lines 1719-1757. They must be deleted (or rewritten per point 1); left as-is they are dead code importing a module #1721 deleted.
